A Xiaohongshu language observation was made separately and stays a draft; none of its words are added. describe() had taken each dimension's words by round index, so only ten distinct words had ever appeared across all 18,432 answer sequences and six of them were on every card. Now: each dimension's owner-approved list starts at a cup-specific offset derived from V_target (consumer terms remain an unrotated tail); the eight slots are shared by dimension weight (one for each of the top three, the rest by largest remainder among dimensions at 12% of the leading weight, at most 1 + floor((words - 1) / 4) per dimension so a three-word list never cycles); the card lists the first word of every dimension before any second word, so the first five positions span five dimensions; picksToVector counts each dimension once. Q6's dimension words are unchanged. Measured after: 59 distinct words, 6,291 main-word triplets, 12,825 distinct eight-word cards, the most frequent word on 39% of cards; Q6 with the first five words 34.2% (unchanged, per path identical to R3-D22), with five words that side with the reader 80.1% (was 63.3%) and with five random words 44.2% (was 20.1%) because strong dimensions now carry two or three words. decisions.decision: Users asked to tap the five progress bars to go back. Each bar stays 4 px thin inside a 40 x 44 px hit box (negative margins keep the row's height), so a finger can hit it. The owner's rule for what happens next: no dialog, and only the reopened question changes — from the fourth question, going back to the first keeps the second and third. Because every question's option ids are fixed and only the prompt's lead-in, the order of the options and the path follow the earlier answers, the answers from the reopened question onward are kept and replayed through the engine once the reader has answered (session.ts: reopenQuestion, answerAndReplay, resumeKept — pure functions; the store holds the kept answers and folds the stack). The flow stops only where the new path asks something never answered, and drops answers it no longer needs. While a question is reopened the option chosen last time is marked, kept questions stay tappable, the bar of the question on screen is taller, and the segment of the question the reader came from returns there with nothing changed (or back to the description when the kept answers complete the flow). After the flow has delivered, the question cards in the stack reopen their question from the description or the final card; words, picks and card are rebuilt from the engine's new result. The owner required proof that the dynamic computation stays exact: tests/product-vector-v1-edit-replay enumerates every reachable state (one to five answers, three contexts) and requires the session after any edit to be identical — whole state, next card with prompt, ranked options and progress, and the delivered result and description — to a fresh session given the final answers. The exhaustive mode passed on 2026-09-18 with no mismatch: 52,473 single edits, 91,884 jumps between kept questions followed by an edit, 900,519 double edits, 189,492 continued answers, 13,611 no-change returns, and 375,318 edits made after delivery from 16,434 starting points; the default run is a stride of the same cases. Home page: the motif row is drawn anew each time the home page appears — order, turn and colour order of the five simple shapes (half, triangle, circle, quarter, diamond); a first version that added drops, arches, squares and crosses and drew on leaves and bars was rejected by the owner as the kind of shape ruled out before. decisions.decision: Owner review of 关于这段描述: the fixed sentence about the reference being a starting point read as mechanical, the reference line only repeated the reader's own choices, 'your description' was too shallow to add anything, and — not acceptable — the same card showed different statistics in Chinese (washed, 1,819 records) and English (medium-dark, 438), because the choice was seeded by the words' text. Now (notes.ts, templates in presentation.card_notes, statistics in bundle.corpus_stats): the builder computes, for every measured option and for 36 pairs of options with at least 30 shared records, the share of review records that mention each flavor dimension, next to the same share over all 6,516 usable records. The initial reference reads the two most distinctive measured choices against the whole (light roast mentions floral in 38% of records against 27% overall; espresso mentions acidity in 59% against 93%), says when the choices are close to the whole, and names choices that have no review records instead of listing them as if they counted; the fixed sentence is gone. The data notes are statistics that bear on the confirmed words — for each confirmed dimension, the chosen option or pair that says most about it — phrased as support from five points above the whole, as a contrast from five points below ('this part comes from your own impression'), otherwise as on par; dimensions that nearly every record mentions cannot support anything. Two data notes, or one plus a research reference two times in three. The description note says which dimensions the answers raised and lowered against the reference, which words on the card come from that lean and which the reference already had, and what the second look stressed. Every template has three variants in the same order in both languages and the seed holds nothing language-dependent (context, answers' vector, confirmed dimensions, session nonce), so a card says the same thing in both languages — tested over 240 cards including a language switch — while another visit may draw a different supporting statistic. decisions.subject: Similar words on one card: a soft constraint, no fixed cap; development of the dynamic question bank to proceed
decisions.decision: The owner asked whether a card could show highly similar words — several near-identical fruit candidates — and whether that is by design. Measured over 18,432 cards: at the level of dimensions it is by design and holds (no card has more than 4 words of one dimension, 99.7% have at most 3: quotas by weight, the three leading dimensions guaranteed, breadth-first order); inside a dimension nothing prevented near-synonyms and 60% of cards carried at least one pair (蜜桔 + 砂糖橘; 牛奶巧克力 + 榛果巧克力 + 巧克力酱), because similar words sit next to each other in the lists and the rotation takes consecutive words. The cap formula 1 + floor((words − 1) / 4) also grows with the list (fruity: 7 after batch 3), although the weights bind first. The operator proposed fixing the cap at 3. The owner decided against a fixed cap — some coffees really are shaped around one kind of flavor — and for a soft constraint that the questions can override, to be written into the design decisions and the README; then development of the dynamic question bank continues. decisions.subject: No Git LFS: the two large ledgers become xz archives in plain git; the historical replay no longer depends on the machine it runs on
decisions.decision: Before this round was pushed the owner allowed the two-clean-database replay (the 18th stage) to be run locally. It failed at the Round 3I freeze check — eight exported inventories hashed differently from the registered values — and failed identically on a clean checkout of main (9b8f311), so the failure was not this round's. Owner: fix it. Cause, in the export script itself: (1) rows were ordered by text under the database's default collation; the registered bytes carry glibc's en_US.utf8 order, which ignores punctuation and spaces at the first level, and macOS orders the same rows differently; (2) timestamptz values were rendered in the session's time zone, the registered bytes are UTC. Fix: the export names its order explicitly — an ICU collation with punctuation ignored (und-u-ka-shifted), ties by byte order, created in pg_temp so the replay database's schema and guard counts are untouched — and sets the session to UTC. Checked against the committed inventories inside a rolled-back transaction: the registered order of all of them is reproduced, the 14,532-row language corpus included; the re-run replay reproduces the registered manifest hash 10ed5e29…aa3991e. Frozen files, migrations and registered hashes are unchanged. Then the owner reported that the account's Git LFS quota is used up until October and that depending on LFS for every update is not acceptable ('这是必须要解决的'). The two source-assertion ledgers (100.8 MB and 109.9 MB, the only LFS objects, there because of GitHub's 100 MiB file limit) cost about 211 MB of LFS bandwidth on every database job; once the bandwidth is gone the job cannot even check the repository out, and the scheduled replay had already been failing since the move to LFS because its postgres container has no git for an LFS checkout. Now: the ledgers are stored as xz archives in plain git (4.7 MB and 5.2 MB); db/scripts/materialize-large-ledgers.py writes them back and verifies size and SHA-256 against LARGE_LEDGER_ARCHIVES.tsv — the hashes equal the former LFS object ids, so every reader, hash contract and the replay see the same bytes; the ledgers themselves are git-ignored. The workflows check out without LFS and run the script; db/scripts/ci-verify.sh runs it first, so a fresh clone works locally as well. The product-layer builders added this round join the CI path filter's exclusions, as the owner ruled on 2026-09-17 that product changes do not re-run the database. Vercel never used LFS (documented as off).
